description.narrative: Sveriges kommuner och regioner (SKR) har till Sida ansökt om finansiellt stöd, uppgående till 16,7 milj. sv. kr., för att genomföra ett projekt, benämnt «Support to Decentralisation and Local Self-Government Reform in Armenia», under perioden juli 2022 - december 2023 (etapp 1). Syftet med projektet är att praktiskt kapacitetsstärka det armeniska kommunförbundet, och att genomföra insatser i ett antal pilotkommuner, baserade på en svensk modell för utveckling av lokalt självstyre, och utveckla en långsiktig «roadmap» för utveckling av relationer på demokratisk grund mellan kommunledning och lokalbefolkning, samt utveckling av en kommunal infrastruktur av tillhandahållna tjänster

The Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions (SALAR) has applied to Sida for financial support, amounting to SEK 16.7 million. Swed. Cr., to implement a project, entitled «Support to decentralization and Local Self-Government Reform in Armenia», during the period July 2022 - December 2023 (stage 1). The aim of the project is to practically capacity-enhance the Union of Municipalities of Armenia, and to carry out actions in a number of pilot municipalities, based on a Swedish model for the development of local self-government, and develop a long-term «roadmap» for the development of relations on a democratic basis between municipal management and the local population, as well as the development of a municipal infrastructure of services provided

The overall objective of the project is to enhance commitment, capacity, and trust among national and local stakeholders for decentralisation and local self-government reforms in Armenia. It will aim to foster a multi-level policy dialogue as a cross-cutting pathway of change, informed by evidence on institutional conditions and capacities at the local level, and underscored by concrete experiences of improving local self-governance practices.
SALAR focuses its interventions on fiscal decentralisation, decentralisation in the field of education and contributes to objectives linked with wider awareness raising, advocacy and strengthening of strategic reform leadership.
Outcome 1. Institutional framework for decentralisation: actors across levels have aligned in their understanding of the decentralisation and LSG reforms and are prepared for implementation
Outcome 2. Fiscal decentralisation: through collaboration of all actors, fiscal decentralisation is operationalised for the Armenian context. Capacity, tools and processes to implement fiscal decentralisation co-developed by critical actors.
Outcome 3. Sector decentralisation (from 2024 onward): sector ministry (Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports) and LSGs have strengthened capacity and capabilities for management and delivery of delegated decentralised service functions .

title.narrative: Grant Agreement on Support to Decentralisation and Local -Self Government Reform in Armenia
Support to Local Self-Government Reform in Armenia

description.narrative:
Support to Decentralisation and Local Self-Government Reforms in Armenian project (DeaLoG) actively contributed to the Armenian Governments decentralisation efforts and reforms, including support in the areas of fiscal and education decentralisation. DeaLoG has focused on establishing closer dialogue between and within policy makers at national level, as well as between national and local levels, to ensure both formal and informal dialogue on how to proceed with the decentralisation agenda. The project worked to ensure that the Armenian local governments day-to day needs channeled and communicated to national level decision-makers so that action plans reflect the situation at local level, and progress is supported by lessons learned and best local and international practices.
DeaLoG project provided key comments and feedback on the draft Law on Local Self-Government and draft Decentralisation Strategy. The project also supported national-level authorities in communicating the reform by conducting a needs assessment and developing policy proposals to further refine the communication strategy for decentralisation reform.
The project continued to provide a regular dialogue platform for municipalities through its annual Municipal Forum. The second Municipal Forum was held in February 2025 in Yerevan, bringing together around 90 participants from 52 municipalities, including 27 mayors, 20 deputy mayors and 17 chief secretaries, as well as representatives from five Marz administrations.
A unified online Portal on Decentralisation (www.decentralisation.am) was developed and launched in Sep 2025. The portal has become a unified source of information around the local governance and decentralisation reforms, developments in municipalities and has been used as an important channel for public discussions. The project and MTAI have agreed that the project would maintain the portal during the implementation period, with a sustainability plan for its gradual transfer to the ministry.
Blue Book on Fiscal Decentralisation published by the project in both English and Armenian and disseminated among national and local level stakeholders. Blue Books - https://salarinternational.am/en/page/8/
A Gap Analysis on Fiscal Decentralisation was conducted, and based on its findings, a roadmap aligned with the broader decentralisation agenda was developed and submitted to the Armenian Government for further implementation. The policy proposals developed by the project, and agreed upon with the Ministry of Finance (MoF), provide systematic solutions to the identified gaps in the fiscal decentralisation reform. They outline a phased, three-stage, and balanced reform agenda aimed at strengthening local governments within a coherent national fiscal framework. At a parliamentary session, the Mayor of Yerevan strongly advocated to the government to adopt the recommendations outlined in the fiscal gap analysis that showed that municipalities were significantly under-funded and called for greater emphasis on reform with financing. He presented and advocated for the recommendations outlined in the fiscal gap analysis done by the project to be integrated into the governments fiscal reform to grant municipalities more power to plan their own budgets and bring service provision closer to those who needs it the most.
Governing Together (STYRSAM) methodology, which stands for governance and leadership in collaboration, was developed by SALAR in close cooperation with Swedish municipalities and focuses on strengthening the local governance chain in schools and preschools. The focus is on transparency and accountability in decision-making processes and addresses the possible risk of politicization of school management by elected officials. STYRSAM was well received by the Armenian national stakeholders with both MoESCS and municipalities approving a pilot in selected municipalities.
The project conducted Functional Review of School Management System aiming to analyse the degree of (de)centralisation of administration in the sector and its impact on educational outcomes, as well as to study the roles and responsibilities of various stakeholders, the distribution of functions and competences.
Pilots have been selected jointly with Ministry of Education and DeaLoG project, where the newly constructed school-hubs were proposed by the Ministry and located in already Projects partner municipalities (in total 3 schools in Martiros village (Vayk municipality), Tatev village (Tatev municipality) and Keti village (Akhuryan municipality). The pilots will be implemented within 2-3 years, and in the first phase will incorporate also the STYRSAM (Governing Together) model piloting, which has been developed by SALAR and applied in Swedish municipalities.
